The payload passed in is produced by _compute_table_payload (lines 901-950), which builds coerced_rows via `[[_coerce_cell(row.get(c, "")) for c in columns] for row in rows]` (line 908) — each row list is constructed by iterating over `columns`, so every row always has exactly len(columns) cells, including after the truncation binary search (payload['rows'] = coerced_rows[:lo], still same per-row shape). checklist.claim: The widget renders the escaped `**col:** value` text via renderTextBlock (markdown-it html:false, breaks:true), and the backslash escapes (including \< \& \|) come out as literal characters. The new comment above createMarkdownRenderer states this accurately.
checklist.verify_against: markdown-it backslash-escape rules (CommonMark ASCII punctuation escapes) and renderTextBlock
checklist.verify_hint: renderTextBlock/createMarkdownRenderer in query_results.html; CommonMark escape rules for & and |
checklist.evidence: renderTextBlock (query_results.html:772-785) builds markdownRenderer via createMarkdownRenderer(window.markdownit) which calls markdownit({ html: false, linkify: false, typographer: false, breaks: true }) at line 753, matching the claim. The comment block at lines 740-751 (inside md-renderer:start/end markers) accurately documents html:false as the XSS boundary, no images, validateLink default, and breaks:true for newlines. Server side, src/sqllens/tools/_format.py defines _SMALL_RESULT_ESCAPED_CHARS = frozenset("\\`*_[]<>~|&") (line 49) and _escape_small_result_text (line 1192-1197) backslash-escapes each of those characters, used to build '**col:** value' lines (line 1218). Per CommonMark's backslash-escape rule, any ASCII punctuation character (including & < > | which are all in the ASCII punctuation set) may be backslash-escaped and renders as the literal character rather than being interpreted as markup; markdown-it (a CommonMark-compliant parser) implements exactly this rule. Thus \<, \&, \| all render as literal <, &, | characters through renderTextBlock/createMarkdownRenderer as claimed.

checklist.claim: The comment says escaped characters make database values 'render as literal text rather than Markdown formatting.' Try to falsify it with values the escape set does not cover: a leading '#', '1.', '-', or '+' (headings and lists), '!' before an escaped bracket, a URL (linkify autolinks), or entity-like sequences.
checklist.source_excerpt:
# Characters backslash-escaped in those lines so database values render as
# literal text rather than Markdown formatting.
checklist.verify_against: markdown-it configuration in query_results.html (is linkify enabled?) and CommonMark block syntax
checklist.verify_hint: Construct 1-column values such as '# heading', '1. item', 'http://evil.example', '---' and render them through the widget's markdown-it options. Note: in the single-column case the value follows '**col:** ', so block syntax may not trigger; check the column name too.
checklist.evidence: The escape set _SMALL_RESULT_ESCAPED_CHARS = frozenset("\\`*_[]<>~|&") (src/sqllens/tools/_format.py:49) escapes backslash, backtick, *, _, [, ], <, >, ~, |, &. Falsification vectors checked: (1) '#' heading, '1.' ordered list, '-'/'+' bullet, '---' hr all require being at the START of a Markdown line to trigger block syntax; but _small_result_to_markdown always prefixes each value with a literal '**' (single column, _format.py:1218-1222) or '- **' (multi-column, :1223), so an attacker-controlled column/value never occupies column 0 of the rendered line — block syntax cannot fire even though '#', digits+'.', '-', '+' are absent from the escape set. (2) '!' before an escaped bracket: '!' is not escaped, but '[' and ']' ARE escaped (rendered as \\[ \\]), so markdown-it never parses ![...](...) as an image regardless of the unescaped '!' or unescaped '(' ')'. (3) URL autolink/linkify: query_results.html:753 configures `markdownit({ html: false, linkify: false, typographer: false, breaks: true })` — linkify is explicitly disabled, so bare URLs are not autolinked. (4) entity-like sequences: '&', '<', '>' are all in the escape set, neutralizing HTML-entity/tag-like sequences (consistent with html:false anyway). All tested falsification vectors are blocked by the combination of the escape set and the fixed '**'/'- **' line prefix, so the comment's claim holds.
